chunks: Al-Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of it; he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abi Abdillah, from his fathers, from Ali, peace be upon him:

That whenever he exited the toilet, he would say — 'Praise be to Allah who granted me its pleasure, preserved its nourishment in my body, and removed its harm from me — what a blessing!' — three times.

Then he said: and one should step out with the right foot before the left when exiting, God willing. He mentioned this because of the distinction — previously noted — between exiting mosques and exiting the toilet.

Then he said: It is not permissible to defecate on the banks of rivers, for they are places where people come to drink and purify themselves, and it is not permissible to do therein anything that harms them. Nor is it permissible to defecate on main roads, nor in the courtyards of dwellings. Nor is it permissible under fruit-bearing trees, nor in places where travelers alight, nor in the forecourts of homes. Nor is it permissible in water channels, nor in stagnant water. As for what indicates this [ruling]…
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (AS) recite upon exiting the toilet, and which locations are forbidden for defecation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Ali (AS) would recite a specific three-fold praise of Allah upon exiting the toilet — thanking Him for granting the pleasure of food, preserving its nourishment in the body, and removing its harmful waste — and that one should exit with the right foot first (unlike mosques). It then enumerates locations where defecation is forbidden: riverbanks, main roads, house courtyards, under fruit-bearing trees, travelers' rest stops, water channels, and stagnant water, grounding the prohibitions in communal welfare and ritual purity.
